prompts.text: What food do people around you usually eat with their hands, even when cutlery is nearby?
Tell me about a meal where everybody had a different opinion on the best way to serve it.
A breakfast sold by a street vendor or something your family makes slowly on weekends?
The way people share the last piece of food says a lot about the mood at the table.
You're showing a visitor how to eat a local dish. Which little tip would save them the most confusion?
Which snack tastes better when you buy it fresh from the person making it?
The side dishes at a gathering sometimes tell a better story than the main meal.
Describe a food you only started appreciating after trying somebody else's version.
A busy outdoor food stall with regular customers or a small family kitchen with a secret recipe?
What's an everyday food combination people outside your area tend to find surprising?
What expression do people use around you when something has gone slightly wrong?
Tell me about a phrase you heard all the time as a child and now catch yourself saying.
A visitor takes a local expression too seriously. How would you explain the joke behind it?
A funny saying about being late or a dramatic phrase people use when they're hungry?
Some expressions only make sense when you hear the voice people usually say them in.
What word from your neighbourhood would you struggle to replace with a formal one?
A playful local expression often carries more personality than a neat translation.
Describe the first time somebody explained slang to you and you realised you'd guessed its meaning wrong.
You're making a short guide to everyday phrases for a new neighbour. Which situation deserves its own page?
Is there a familiar phrase people say differently depending on whether they're teasing or being serious?
What happens at almost the same time each day where you live?
Tell me about a familiar street scene you missed when you spent time away from home.
A quiet early-morning street or a lively neighbourhood as shops begin closing?
You sometimes recognise a neighbourhood by the people who show up at the same corners every day.
You're taking a friend on a short walk through your area. Which ordinary stop would you include?
Which local business seems to know everyone by name?
A street's everyday routines often feel more personal than its famous landmarks.
Describe a time a neighbour turned an ordinary day into an unexpected small celebration.
A visitor wants to see the neighbourhood as residents experience it. What time would you suggest they arrive?
What's a small change to your local area that longtime residents still talk about?
What's an outfit people in your area wear for comfort rather than to make an impression?
Tell me about borrowing something traditional to wear and learning how to put it on properly.
A colourful everyday print or a plain outfit with one meaningful accessory?
People often have a favourite outfit for visiting relatives, even when the visit isn't formal.
You're packing for a community event where you've never been before. What would you ask about the dress code?
Which clothing detail reminds you of a particular generation in your family?
Everyday clothing choices reveal local habits without needing to make a grand statement.
Describe seeing an old photograph and recognising a fashion trend people have started wearing again.
A friend wants to wear something from your culture respectfully. Where would you suggest they learn about it?
What style of shoes do you associate with getting ready for a big family gathering?
What's a modest occasion people in your area still find a reason to celebrate?
Tell me about a gathering where the best part happened before the planned activities began.
A spontaneous celebration with neighbours or a family occasion planned weeks ahead?
The first people to arrive at a celebration often end up helping with the final preparations.
You have one hour to help organise a simple community celebration. What would you make sure happens?
What little ritual tells you a party is officially starting?
A good celebration doesn't always need a stage, a programme or matching outfits.
Describe a gathering where somebody's unexpected contribution made everyone smile.
A friend attends your family's celebration for the first time. What part would you explain before it begins?
Which part of a celebration do people seem to enjoy long after the main event ends?
